subject: Private VPC preflight: control/data separation and egress constraints
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@crimson.cloud>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Private VPC preflight (control/data separation)

Hi Karthik —

We’re kicking off a private deployment (Crimson Cloud) for an on-prem inference footprint and want to run a short preflight with the Redwood infra/arch team focused on control-plane / data-plane separation, egress constraints, and crossconnect expectations. High level: 3 racks in their colo, each rack hosts 2x A100-ish inference nodes and a lightweight gateway. They need control-plane calls to be able to (a) reach an ops endpoint for rollouts/metrics and (b) be optionally routed through a customer-managed NAT for egress inspection.

Specific asks:
- Can you confirm the recommended control-plane topology for a private (air-gapped-adjacent) deployment?
- Advice on KV-cache replication and where the control-plane auth tokens should live (customer KMS vs Redwood KMS).
- Egress patterns and a fallback if the colo restricts outbound IPs to a small set.

We’d appreciate a quick readout and an annotated topology sketch. We have a kickoff call Thursday 2026-08-22 14:00 PT — would love to be able to walk a proposal then.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Sr. Infrastructure Eng — Crimson Cloud
Attachment: topology-export-v0.stub (PNG)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@crimson.cloud>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private VPC preflight (control/data separation)

Hi Ellen —

Thanks for the details — copying Irene (networks) and Marissa (deploy ops) so we can prep a concise preflight. I attached an initial annotated topology (redwood-private-topology-v1.pdf) and a short egress matrix spreadsheet we use to map outbound patterns. High-level notes below: 

1) Control-plane topology:
   - We recommend a split control-plane model for on-prem: a small local agent (governed by customer) that handles node lifecycle and KV cache warm-start, and a control-plane management endpoint in a restricted Redwood control plane (TLS mTLS). If you must avoid outbound reachability entirely, we can support a private control-plane proxy that runs in Crimson’s DMZ and brokers signed operations.
2) Auth & KMS:
   - Customer-managed KMS for secret material is preferred for regulated workloads. We can accept signed keys/certs (JWK) and will store short-lived tokens in our control-plane; keys remain in customer KMS. If that isn’t workable we can propose a hybrid — customer wraps a signing key and we exchange ephemeral credentials.
3) KV cache / state:
   - Local KV-cache per inference node with periodic snapshotting to an S3-compatible endpoint located in the customer VPC. Cross-rack replication is optional (adds write complexity).
4) Egress / NAT constraints:
   - We can constrain control-plane egress to a narrow IP set and provide a pinned TLS certificate for your firewall allowlist. For metrics and telemetry you can route through your NAT/inspection appliance; we’ll support HTTP(S) proxy env vars on the agent.

Open questions for the call:
- Do you need full offline air-gap (no external outbound)?
- What crossconnect type (L2/L3/VPN) will the colo provide?
- Will you accept our pinned IPs or prefer domain-based TLS allowlisting?

Attachment: redwood-private-topology-v1.pdf (annotated)
Attachments: onprem-egress-matrix.csv

If you’re good, we’ll propose a 20-minute readout for Thursday and bring a minimal checklist (control-plane endpoints, firewall rules, KMS thumbprints, S3-compatible endpoint).

—Karthik
Director, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Ellen Park <ellen@crimson.cloud>
Date: 2026-08-22T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private VPC preflight (control/data separation)

Quick infra review notes ahead of the call — pulled together by the network team.

A) Control-plane reachability patterns we prefer:
   - Primary: mTLS to our managed control-plane over egress port 443 with static IP allowlist.
   - Secondary (air-gap-friendly): local broker in customer DMZ that accepts signed operations and queues them to local agents (we provide a small VM image + TLS materials).

B) Egress & NAT:
   - If Crimson requires outbound inspection, the gateway should perform SNI passthrough (not TLS termination) for control-plane calls. If termination is required by your security team, we will need a mutual cert rotation cadence documented and an API key exchange plan.

C) Observability:
   - Metric shipping can be buffered and forwarded by the local gateway to your telemetry endpoint. Please confirm retention/PII requirements — we will not persist raw customer prompts.

D) Network recommendations (short):
   - Use BGP or static routes for the colo crossconnect; prefer /29 for control-plane egress ranges.
   - NAT mapping: consistent SNAT is critical for firewall pinning.

I attached a small notes file with our suggested firewall rules and the agent bootstrap sequence.

Attachment: controlplane-ops-notes.txt

I’ll cover the above on the call and annotate the PDF in real time.

—Irene
Sr. Network Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Ellen Park <ellen@crimson.cloud>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private VPC preflight (control/data separation)

Thanks — this looks good. We don’t need a fully air-gapped deploy (we have a DMZ NAT that inspects outbound), so the pinned-IP + SNI passthrough pattern should be workable. Two quick clarifications before the call: 
- Can you provide the IP ranges you intend to pin so our security team can start firewall requests?
- For KMS: we’ll likely prefer the customer-managed KMS option. I’ll bring the KMS owner to the call.

Call confirmed for Thu 14:00 PT (we scheduled on your calendar). Please keep the readout to 20 minutes; we’ll use the remaining 40 for the Crimson ops folks to ask follow-ups.

Cheers,
Ellen
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, Ellen Park <ellen@crimson.cloud>
Date: 2026-08-22T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private VPC preflight (control/data separation)

Ack — I’ll bring the deploy-runbook checklist and the IP allowlist template (we can prefill once we have the exact ranges). Also will prepare the minimal bootstrap steps for the agent so Crimson can validate in a dev rack before the staging cutover.

Attachments: deploy-runbook-template.md

—Marissa
Manager, Deployment Ops — Redwood Inference
